content: Conflict of Interest Declarations and Management 1. Kristin Aunan: No conflicts of interest declared. 2. Kalpana Balakrishnan: No conflicts of interest declared. 3. John Balmes: No conflicts of interest declared. 4. Michael Bates: Declared a conflict of interest. He received a research grant from the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) between 2010 and 2016 to study tuberculosis risk factors and fuel use. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was deemed necessary. 5. Michael Brauer: Declared conflicts of interest. He receives annual income from the Health Effects Institute for serving on the Review Committee of the International Scientific Oversight Committee. He has also received grants and honoraria from the British Columbia Lung Association and a fellowship award from the East-West Centre. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 6. Kenneth Bryden: No conflicts of interest declared. 7. Aaron Cohen: No conflicts of interest declared. 8. He is employed by an organization that conducts monitoring and evaluation of household energy programs in developing regions. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 16. Claudio Lanata: Declared a conflict of interest. He received financial support from the Optimus Foundation for a randomized controlled trial (RCT) involving cookstoves in Peru. Hisham Zerriffi: Declared conflicts of interest. He received non-monetary support, including stoves and customer details, during an emissions monitoring study from a cookstove company in India (First Energy). He also received non-monetary support in the form of emissions testing equipment loans from colleagues at the University of Minnesota and North Carolina State University. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 32. Randy Elder: No conflicts of interest declared. 33. Jill Baumgartner: No conflicts of interest declared. 34. Tami Bond: Declared conflicts of interest. She received financial support from the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for stove emissions measurements, as well as funding from the US National Science Foundation, Department of Energy, and NASA for climate change research. She also received an honorarium for speaking at a Health Effects Institute Conference and provided testimony to US House of Representatives committees on the role of black carbon in climate change (2007 and 2010). This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 35. Judy Guernsey: Declared conflicts of interest. She received per diem compensation (2010–2011) and research study contracts (2009–2011) from Health Canada. She also received indoor air quality monitoring equipment loans from Perkin-Elmer (2009–2011). This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 36. Andrew Grieshop: No conflicts of interest declared. 37. Morgan de Foort: Declared conflicts of interest. He worked as a research and development consultant for a stove manufacturing company, Envirofit, and as a technical consultant to the Global Alliance for Clean Cookstoves. He also receives funds from a patent registered under Colorado State University. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 38. Jacob Kithinji: Declared conflicts of interest. He received financial support from the Global Alliance for Clean Cookstoves and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to establish a cookstove laboratory in Nairobi. He also chairs the Appropriate Technology Technical Committee at the Kenya Bureau of Standards, which is responsible for setting stove standards for the next six months. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 39. Ryan Allen: No conflicts of interest declared. 40. Rogelio Perez-Padilla: No conflicts of interest declared. 41. Ranyee Chiang: Declared a conflict of interest. She is employed by a public–private alliance/foundation involved in research, testing, and market approaches to improve health, environment, and livelihoods through cooking technologies and fuels. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 51. Veena Joshi: No conflicts of interest declared. 52. Christoph Messinger: Declared a conflict of interest. He has a salaried contract with the Energizing Development Program/Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), which has an interest in the outcomes of the indoor air quality guidelines as they may influence programmatic decisions. This was reviewed by the WHO Secretariat, and no action was required. 53. Mike Sage: No conflicts of interest declared. This list provides a detailed account of conflicts of interest declared by individuals involved in the WHO Indoor Air Quality Guidelines development process, along with the actions taken (or not required) by the WHO Secretariat.
